front: Turning point of f′ corresponds to…?
back: A point of inflexion of f.
The derivative of $f'$: $f''(x) = \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ — the rate of change of the gradient.
Up (cup): gradient increasing, $f'' > 0$. Down (cap): gradient decreasing, $f'' < 0$.

front: On the graph of $f'$, what do the $x$-intercepts show about $f$?
back: Stationary points of $f$ (where its gradient is 0) — not zeros of $f$.

front: How do you identify a maximum of $f$ from the graph of $f'$?
back: $f'$ crosses the $x$-axis from positive to negative. (Negative to positive: a minimum.)

front: What does it mean for $f$ where the graph of $f'$ is increasing?

back: Zeros of $f'$ give stationary points; the sign of $f'$ gives increasing/decreasing; turning points of $f'$ give inflexion points of $f$.
Acceleration — the rate of change of velocity.
